acceptance_criteria.source: The `/changelog` command invoked at turn 0 cuts a release section from Unreleased; CHANGELOG.md follows Keep a Changelog, whose release headings are `## [version] - date`.
acceptance_criteria.text: In CHANGELOG.md the `## [Unreleased]` heading is replaced by a versioned, dated release heading in the file's existing form (`## [X.Y.Z] - YYYY-MM-DD`), with the Unreleased content kept under it.

acceptance_criteria.source: /changelog skill (.claude/skills/changelog): format `- Description ([#N](...))` and 'No trailing period on bullet items'
acceptance_criteria.text: Every bullet in the new release section ends with a PR link in the changelog's existing format (`([#N](https://github.com/entireio/git-sync/pull/N))`), with no period before the link.

acceptance_criteria.source: The `/changelog` command prescribes sweeping merged PRs (the assistant cites 'the `git log --merges` sweep the skill prescribes') and adding missing entries.
acceptance_criteria.text: Every PR merged since the previous release that had no changelog entry is represented in the new release section (in the session these were #104 and #105), identified from the merge history and GitHub PR list when reachable, or from the repository's git history alone with a note that GitHub could not be reached.

acceptance_criteria.source: Cutting a changelog release section is a documentation-only task; touching other files would be unrelated change.
acceptance_criteria.text: Only CHANGELOG.md is modified; no other files change.

acceptance_criteria.source: "yeah please compress them" in answer to the offer to compress the security bullets.
acceptance_criteria.text: The Security bullets in the new release section are noticeably shorter than the Unreleased text they came from.

acceptance_criteria.source: Compression means shortening prose, not dropping entries; losing an entry or its attribution would break the changelog the user asked to tighten.
acceptance_criteria.text: Compressing the Security bullets removes no entry and no PR link: every Security entry present before compression is still present with its PR link(s).

acceptance_criteria.source: "mentioning go-git twice in security and housekeeping 🤔"
acceptance_criteria.text: The go-git dependency bump is described in only one place in the release section, not once under Security and again under Housekeeping.

acceptance_criteria.source: Removing a duplicate mention must not drop the PR attribution that the `/changelog` back-fill requires; the fix is to merge, not to lose a citation.
acceptance_criteria.text: After consolidating the go-git mention, both PRs behind it (#105 and #106) are still cited in the release section, so no merged PR loses attribution.

analysis.completion_evidence: Final diff shows `## [0.9.0] - 2026-08-28`, every Security bullet ending in a PR link, a new #104 x/crypto bullet, the go-git bullet citing both #105 and #106, bullets visibly shortened versus the removed text, and Security followed directly by Added with no Housekeeping section. Only CHANGELOG.md appears in the diff.
analysis.notes: Edits were made via shell commands (Bash), so 'Files touched: none' is misleading; the diff shows CHANGELOG.md changed. analysis.task_statement: Run the project's `/changelog` skill to cut a new release section in CHANGELOG.md: rename the Unreleased section to a versioned, dated heading, back-fill PR links on every bullet, and add entries for any merged PRs missing from the changelog. Follow-ups asked to compress the overly long Security bullets and to remove a duplicate mention of the go-git bump that appeared in two sections.

turn_script.intent: Yes, compress the long Security bullets in the new release section.
turn_script.skip_if: The replay's Security bullets are already concise, or the replay never produces a release section.
turn_script.trigger: The replay has produced the release section and asks or offers whether the security bullets should be shortened, or presents them at their original very long length.

turn_script.intent: The go-git bump should not be mentioned in two different sections; consolidate it so it appears once.
turn_script.skip_if: The go-git bump is mentioned in only one place in the release section.
turn_script.trigger: The replay's release section mentions the go-git bump in more than one section (e.g. both Security and Housekeeping).
